doc_name: President of the Supreme Federal Court
text: The President of the Supreme Federal Court is the highest-ranking official in the Brazilian judiciary and also serves as president of the National Council of Justice (CNJ). Their duties include representing both the Court and the CNJ before other branches of government and authorities, presiding over plenary sessions of both bodies, enforcing their bylaws, deciding points of order during sessions, ruling on injunctions when the institutions are in recess or vacation, and administering oaths to Supreme Court justices and CNJ councillors. The President is fourth in the Brazilian presidential line of succession and presides over all federal impeachment trials. The President and Vice President of the Supreme Court are elected by their peers via a secret ballot, requiring a quorum of at least eight justices, using a two-round system, and serve a single, non-renewable two-year term. Historically, a tradition of rotation has existed, where the most senior justice who has not yet served becomes President and the second-most senior becomes Vice President, though this practice is not codified by law. Self-governance in selecting the Court’s president was absent during two periods: under the monarchy, when the Emperor appointed the President for a renewable three-year term; and under the 1937 Constitution, when the President of Brazil appointed the Court’s President from among the current justices for an indefinite term. The longest presidency lasted 13 years and 312 days, held by Hermínio do Espírito Santo, while the shortest lasted 23 days, held by Leoni Ramos. The current President is Justice Edson Fachin, who has held the position since 29 September 2025.
